references.observation: The 2020 Beijing TV photograph shows a broad tile roof, deep wooden porch, glazed central doors and side windows, irregular stone infill below the window sills and a narrow stair in the paved approach.
The 2018 terrace photograph shows the Water Village tea-house sign, the recessed walls and the same irregular stone patches beneath the windows.
The park photograph shows the gate and south-range tea-room facade on the same approach.
Photograph 8 on printed page 34 shows masonry gable ends under the dark projecting tiles in the 2003 Water Village landscape. The picture describes the group and does not label individual footprints.
The winter aerial shows the roof ridges running along the long axes of the two PMTiles rear ranges. The east range has straight ridge and eave lines and a squared west end.

visualBrief: Grey tiled halls, red timber frames, green lattice screens and pale stone thresholds surround the Water Training School courts. A sheltered southern gallery and separate waterside structures sit above the native pond. The Water Village court to the north has grey tiles, broad dark timber and glass doors, and low stone sills. The south range has a recessed veranda with irregular stone under the windows and a narrow central stair. A short walk and stone landing join the south-range approach to the veranda. Recessed masonry gables close the ends of the two rear ranges under the roofs.
nativeAxes: +X and +Z are mapped local axes. Building bearings are derived independently from their mapped outlines.

waterVillageSouthRange.attribution: tea-room and south approach shown by park photograph
waterVillageSouthRange.observation: The south range has a recessed timber-and-glass front, an open veranda, irregular stone infill and a narrow central step. The paved strip in the aerial view matches the approach through the gate in the park photograph. The exact gate setback remains approximate.
